messages:
amelia: Heads-up — customer ran into a slow path converting legacy tarball checkpoints that already bundle .safetensors. Our loader either extracts the whole tar (double-copy) or streams but can't mmap. Thinking about a compact compatibility shim: generate a small index file (\.sidx) that maps each safetensors entry -> byte range in the tar + sha256. Loader could then do HTTP range reads and mmap trusted stores.

ravi: hmm, where does sidx live? next to the tar in object store? generated at upload time or lazily at first access?

amelia: ideal is upload-time in the ingestion pipeline for enterprise customers. Hosted customers can have lazy generation on first read. Also cache sidx in metadata service to avoid repeated scans.

tony: tradeoffs: CPU cost for tar scanning + hashing, potential staleness if object replaced, and security risk if an index is forged.

maria: make sidx refer to object ETag/sha and fail closed: if object hash != sidx.ref then ignore it and fall back to full stream/extract. sidx should be signed for hosted runs.

jasper: +1 on signing. Also consider small tensor optimization: if tensor < N bytes inline it into a tiny manifest to avoid a separate range request. Cuts round trips for many tiny tensors.

deploy-bot: note — indexing large tarballs will spike CPU at ingestion. Recommend async job + quotas.

ravi: another nuance: tars may contain pre-sharded safetensors (model.safetensors.part-0, part-1...). sidx needs to preserve file boundaries and ordering so our WeightSource can reconstruct logical shards.

amelia: agreed — sidx entry should include: file_name, start, end, compressed_flag, sha256, logical_shard_id, order_idx. That way loader knows how to request parts and parallelize warmup.

tony: rough implementation plan: (1) index-generator lib (Rust/C++) used by ingestion and the CLI, (2) store a tiny metadata record linking tar->sidx with etag + signer, (3) loader path that prefers sidx range reads + mmap and falls back to streaming/extract if missing or verification fails. Version sidx schema as v1.

maria: monitoring metrics to add: percent of loads served via sidx, average prefetch latency for range reads, CPU-hours used to build indexes, and bytes saved by range reads vs full extraction.

jasper: tests: fuzz corrupted sidx, simulate a race where sidx exists but tar replaced mid-upload, ensure loader refuses to mmap wrong offsets. Add a safety gate: verification read of the first 1-4KB of the target range and compare a stored hash prefix before mmap.

ravi: perf detail for large layers: quantized .bin blobs are sensitive to page alignment. sidx should either store page-aligned offsets or the generator should round to OS page boundaries and record inner offsets so loader can slice without copying.

amelia: generator can round start down to page boundary and end up to page boundary and store inner_offsets for exact slicing. Document that small header misalignments may incur a short copy.

tony: security policy: hosted requires sidx signature by our ingestion signer; private/customer-managed deployments may allow unsigned sidx if ingestion is customer-controlled.

maria: action items: draft sidx JSON schema, CLI flags for generator (chunk-size, page-align, inline-threshold, sign-key), migration plan (background reindex existing customer tars), and a lifecycle job to delete stale sidx when object is replaced.

amelia: I'll draft the RFC with schema example and perf targets. Want to keep the shim minimal to reduce blast radius.

jasper: I can own a POC next week. I'll build a small generator + python loader shim to validate on a couple of sample tarballs.

ravi: I'll pair on integration tests and ensure the warmup logic uses sidx to prioritize large dense tensors first for KV cache seeding.

maria: cc infra on ingestion CPU quotas and async job design. Also please add metrics to the console for adoption tracking. Thanks all :rocket:
